topics.title: Why Cats Can't Taste Sweetness
topics.central_fact: Domestic cats carry an unexpressed Tas1r2 pseudogene, so the two-part sweet-taste receptor cannot form.

topics.title: The Guilty Look Isn't Guilt
topics.central_question: Does a dog's guilty look mean the dog feels guilty?
topics.central_fact: A dog's guilty look is influenced by owner cues and scolding, not by whether the dog actually disobeyed.

topics.title: Why a Dog's Nose Works in Stereo
topics.central_question: How does a dog's nose separate smelling from breathing?
topics.central_fact: A computer model built from MRI scans showed that a dog's nasal airflow splits into separate olfactory and respiratory paths, and each nostril samples a spatially separate patch of air.

topics.title: The Muscle Behind Puppy-Dog Eyes
topics.central_question: Why do dogs have that expressive inner-eyebrow look?
topics.central_fact: Dogs have a facial muscle that raises the inner eyebrow, and the dogs studied produced that movement more often and intensely than wolves.

topics.title: The Cry Hidden in a Cat's Purr
topics.central_question: Why does a hungry cat's purr sound so urgent?
topics.central_fact: In a 2009 study, solicitation purrs contained a pronounced high-frequency component around 380 Hz, and listeners rated them more urgent and less pleasant than ordinary purrs.

topics.title: What a Cat's Slow Blink Really Means
topics.central_question: Do cats understand a human slow blink?
topics.central_fact: In two experiments, cats showed more eye narrowing and half-blinks when a human slow-blinked at them, and they were more likely to approach an unfamiliar experimenter after a slow blink.
